findings.issue_text: slots.ts:113 — `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object references so it is always false; the empty-override (start === end, day fully blocked) check never fires and such slots are treated as available
slots.ts:141-146 — `start` and `end` are both computed from `slotStartTime`; the slot's end time is never checked, so a slot ending after `workingHour.endTime` is accepted as available

slots.ts:139-146 — `workingHours.find` rejects the slot as soon as any single working-hours entry for the weekday doesn't contain it; with multiple ranges on one day a slot inside one range is wrongly rejected. Should reject only if no matching range contains the slot

slots.ts:140 — `slotStartTime` is UTC but `workingHour.startTime/endTime/days` are in the organizer's timezone; comparing UTC hour-of-day/day-of-week against local working hours gives wrong results for non-UTC organizers and can shift the weekday across midnight

slots.ts:105-111 — `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` is applied to `dayjs(date.start)` parsed in process-local timezone, so the 'YYYY MM DD' date-match comparison against UTC `slotStartTime` depends on the server's TZ setting

slots.ts:105-135 — `dateOverrides.find` is order-dependent: callback returns undefined for a contained slot and true for a non-contained one, so with two overrides on the same day a slot inside the second override is rejected by the first

slots.ts:103-135 — `dateOverrides` are flattened across all users with `userId` but `checkIfIsAvailable` ignores `userId`, so for collective/round-robin events one host's date override is applied to every host's availability check

packages/lib/slots.ts:211-214 — `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses `Date.prototype.toString()` output, which is not an ISO format dayjs supports; can yield Invalid Date and NaN offsets. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly

packages/lib/slots.ts:211 — `override.timeZone` is optional; when undefined `.tz(undefined)` resolves to the process default timezone, silently producing a wrong offset for callers other than `getSchedule`

packages/lib/slots.ts:211-221 — overrides whose offset shifts them across UTC midnight compute `startTime`/`endTime` as minute-of-day only, so an end wrapping past midnight becomes smaller than the start, producing an inverted/empty range matched against the wrong calendar day

slots.ts:492,517 — `...schedule` spreads per-user `dateOverrides` while `...availabilityCheckProps` spreads the flattened all-user list; whichever comes last wins, and here the aggregated cross-user list overrides the per-user one, compounding the userId-ignoring issue
slots.ts:105-135 — inside the per-slot hot loop each override recomputes `dayjs.tz(date.start, tz)` and constructs 4–6 new dayjs objects; precompute per-override UTC bounds once outside the slot loop

getSchedule.test.ts:788-804 — new test only covers an invitee timezone (+6:00) against a UTC organizer; it does not cover a non-UTC organizer, empty (start === end) overrides, multiple overrides on the same day, or the new working-hours rejection path

packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5 — `timeZone?: string` added to the generic `TimeRange` type with no comment on when it is populated; only `getSchedule` sets it, so other producers leave it undefined and hit the `.tz(undefined)` path

adjudication_records.issue_text: slots.ts:139-146 — `workingHours.find` rejects the slot as soon as any single working-hours entry for the weekday doesn't contain it; with multiple ranges on one day a slot inside one range is wrongly rejected. Should reject only if no matching range contains the slot

slots.ts:140 — `slotStartTime` is UTC but `workingHour.startTime/endTime/days` are in the organizer's timezone; comparing UTC hour-of-day/day-of-week against local working hours gives wrong results for non-UTC organizers and can shift the weekday across midnight

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`, `checkIfIsAvailable` sets `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then checks working hours via `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` and computes `start/end` from `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()`. `WorkingHours.days/startTime/endTime` represent local schedule/organizer time (minutes since local midnight and local weekday), but the code compares them against UTC weekday/hour, without converting `time`/`slotStartTime` into the organizer (or working-hours) timezone. This will misclassify slots for non-UTC timezones and can shift the weekday across midnight. The diff even introduces `organizerTimeZone` but only uses it for date overrides, not for the working-hours check, reinforcing that this mismatch is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: slots.ts:105-111 — `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` is applied to `dayjs(date.start)` parsed in process-local timezone, so the 'YYYY MM DD' date-match comparison against UTC `slotStartTime` depends on the server's TZ setting

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is explicitly coerced to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc()`), but the date-override comparison uses `dayjs(date.start)` / `dayjs(date.end)` without `.utc()` or `.tz(...)`. Since `date.start` is a `Date`, `dayjs(date.start)` will interpret/format it in the process-local timezone. The code then adds an offset derived from `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and compares `format("YYYY MM DD")` against a UTC-formatted `slotStartTime`. That means the day-boundary check can change depending on the server's TZ setting (because the base `dayjs(date.start)` is local-time), so the finding correctly identifies a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: slots.ts:105-135 — `dateOverrides.find` is order-dependent: callback returns undefined for a contained slot and true for a non-contained one, so with two overrides on the same day a slot inside the second override is rejected by the first

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` when the slot is *outside* an override interval on the same day (e.g., `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end...)` or `slotEndTime <= date.start...`). Because `.find` stops at the first `true`, if there are multiple overrides on the same day, an earlier override that does not contain the slot will cause `.find` to succeed and the function to `return false`, even if a later override would contain the slot. This makes the result depend on override ordering and can incorrectly reject valid slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: slots.ts:103-135 — `dateOverrides` are flattened across all users with `userId` but `checkIfIsAvailable` ignores `userId`, so for collective/round-robin events one host's date override is applied to every host's availability check

adjudication.rationale: In `getSchedule`, `dateOverrides` are built by `userAvailability.flatMap(...)` and each override is tagged with `{ userId, timeZone, ...override }` (viewer/slots.ts ~408). However, `checkIfIsAvailable`’s `dateOverrides` parameter type is only `{ start: Date; end: Date; }[]` and its logic iterates `dateOverrides.find(...)` without filtering by `userId` (viewer/slots.ts ~99-155). All calls to `checkIfIsAvailable` pass the same aggregated `availabilityCheckProps` (containing the flattened overrides) for checks that are per-schedule/per-user (e.g., for each `schedule` / `userSchedule.timeZone`). As a result, one host’s date override can cause `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false` for slots being evaluated for a different host in collective/round-robin contexts. The diff shows no filtering step, so the finding is a real correctness issue introduced/left in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:211-214 — `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses `Date.prototype.toString()` output, which is not an ISO format dayjs supports; can yield Invalid Date and NaN offsets. Use `dayjs(override.start)` directly

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` (and same for invitee). `override.start` is a `Date`, but converting it to `Date.prototype.toString()` yields a locale/engine-dependent, non-ISO string (e.g. includes timezone name), which Dayjs will parse via the JS Date string parser and can produce `Invalid Date` in some environments. That would make `utcOffset()` return `NaN` and break the offset math. Using `dayjs(override.start)` (passing the Date object directly) avoids this parsing risk and is the correct/safer approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:211 — `override.timeZone` is optional; when undefined `.tz(undefined)` resolves to the process default timezone, silently producing a wrong offset for callers other than `getSchedule`

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new logic computes `organizerUtcOffset` as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `override.timeZone` is optional (made `timeZone?: string` in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`). There is no guard/fallback when it’s `undefined`, so the offset calculation will depend on how `dayjs.tz()` handles an undefined timezone (either defaulting or erroring), which can yield incorrect slot calculations for any `activeOverrides` entries lacking `timeZone` (e.g., callers not populating it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:211-221 — overrides whose offset shifts them across UTC midnight compute `startTime`/`endTime` as minute-of-day only, so an end wrapping past midnight becomes smaller than the start, producing an inverted/empty range matched against the wrong calendar day

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `packages/lib/slots.ts` computes each override’s `startTime`/`endTime` as “minute-of-day” after applying an offset (`dayjs(...).utc().add(offset,"minute").hour()*60 + minute`). If the offset moves one boundary across UTC midnight (e.g., a local same-day override becomes 23:00–00:30 in the shifted UTC day), `endTime` can become numerically smaller than `startTime` even though the override is a continuous interval. There is no handling for wraparound or day association in this representation, so downstream code that assumes `startTime <= endTime` will treat it as inverted/empty or match it against the wrong day. This is a real correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: slots.ts:492,517 — `...schedule` spreads per-user `dateOverrides` while `...availabilityCheckProps` spreads the flattened all-user list; whichever comes last wins, and here the aggregated cross-user list overrides the per-user one, compounding the userId-ignoring issue
slots.ts:105-135 — inside the per-slot hot loop each override recomputes `dayjs.tz(date.start, tz)` and constructs 4–6 new dayjs objects; precompute per-override UTC bounds once outside the slot loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add multiple `dayjs(...)` constructions inside `checkIfIsAvailable` while iterating `dateOverrides` (and this function is called per candidate slot), so the observation about repeated object creation is grounded. However, this is a performance optimization suggestion, not a verifiable correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the diff: nothing in the change demonstrates it causes an actual failure or unacceptable regression, and “precompute outside the slot loop” is speculative without evidence/benchmarks.
